about: Fictional walkthrough seat (ops/make-demo-map.py). Not a real person.
name: Sam Rivera

map.title: Your map
map.law: Every step either clears a likely bottleneck or tells us more about one.

phases.label: Tell us more
phases.pace: A few minutes each; every answer sharpens the map

phases.label: The course
phases.pace: In order, at your pace: each step has its film and its tasks

nodes.title: Get your profile ready for the notes
nodes.why: While we work on the rest, this is the one thing that moves today. It takes about ten minutes, and only you can do it.

because: You've sent 76 to 200 applications and rarely hear back.

video.title: Today's ten minutes, done on screen
video.summary: Your coach does one of these ten-minute steps, start to finish, so you can see what done looks like.

how: Open your LinkedIn profile and click the pencil beside your name.
Start the headline with the exact title you want, written the way postings write it, for example "Backend Engineer".
After a bar, add what you work on in a few words: the kind of system, the languages.
Leave out "open to work", "seeking" and "aspiring". The title already says it.
Save, then open your profile in a private window and read the top line as a stranger would.
nodes.example: Backend Engineer | Payment and data APIs in Python and Go

tasks.title: Change your LinkedIn headline so it names the role you want
tasks.done_when: Your headline names the role you want.
tasks.changed: A hiring manager who opens your profile from a note now reads the role you want first.

nodes.title: 1 role picked for you
nodes.why: A taste of the full plan: one fresh role that fits what you told us, what to lead with, and a note you can send. On the full plan this happens every week.

sample.title: Backend Engineer, Payments
lead: Six years running payment and data APIs in Python and Go, which is the core of this role.
The billing service you owned: say what it handled and what you changed about it.
Postgres in production, since the listing asks for it by name.
sample.fit: A strong fit on the backend and payments work. The listing mentions Kafka, which your resume doesn't show; leave it out rather than stretch.

note.subject: Backend Engineer, Payments: six years on payment APIs
note.body:
Hi,

I saw the Backend Engineer, Payments role at Larkspur Pay. For six years I've built and run payment and data APIs in Python and Go, most recently a billing service I owned end to end.

I've applied through your site. If it's useful, I'm happy to walk through how I'd approach your payments stack in a short call.

Thanks,
Sam Rivera

tasks.title: Read the role, then apply and send the note if it fits
tasks.done_when: You've applied, or decided it doesn't fit.
tasks.changed: One fresh role has your application, led with what fits.

nodes.evidence: One fresh role has your application, led with what fits.

nodes.title: Build your resume, one question at a time
nodes.why: Hiring software checks each required skill against your lines, and a recruiter skims the top in seconds. Specific, checkable lines are what still stand out now that anyone can polish a resume with AI.
nodes.evidence: A downloaded resume where you confirmed every line.

tasks.title: Answer the questions and confirm every line
how: Bring the resume you have. The builder reads every line and lists what a reader would miss, one question at a time.
Answer what you can and skip the rest. Everything you say is kept.
Writing the new lines and downloading the resume is part of GridSchool Complete.
tasks.done_when: Every line on your resume is confirmed.
tasks.changed: Every line on your resume is one you confirmed, and your role reads and campaigns now work from it.

tasks.title: Download it as Word and PDF
tasks.done_when: You have the Word file and the PDF saved where you apply from.
tasks.changed: You have a Word file and a PDF of a resume you can explain line by line.

nodes.title: Get your applications in front of a person
nodes.why: Portal applications are skimmed by software and busy recruiters. A short note to the person hiring is read.

because: You've sent 76 to 200 applications and rarely hear back.

nodes.prepared: We find five fresh roles that fit you, who to look for on each team, and a short note to the hiring manager in your voice.

tasks.title: Send the five notes from your own LinkedIn
tasks.changed: Five hiring managers now have a note from you, not only a portal application.

video.title: What we prepare, and what to check before it goes out
video.summary: Your coach opens a finished piece of prepared work, reads it the way you should, and shows what to check before anything goes out under your name.

nodes.evidence: Five notes have gone to hiring managers.

nodes.title: Make your resume read like the role you want
nodes.why: A reader decides in a few seconds whether you fit. The first lines have to say the role and the proof.

because: Most replies depend on a quick skim of your resume, and right now those replies aren't coming.
In your resume, your bullet points describe your duties, not what changed because of your work.
In your resume, there are no numbers that show the impact of your work.

nodes.prepared: We rewrite your headline and the top of your resume from what you've told us, and flag any number we need you to confirm.

tasks.title: Confirm or correct the facts we flagged
tasks.done_when: Every flagged fact is confirmed or fixed.
tasks.changed: Every number in your new top lines is one you've checked.

tasks.title: Put the new top lines on your resume and LinkedIn
tasks.done_when: Your resume and LinkedIn show the new top lines.
tasks.changed: Your resume and LinkedIn now open with the role you want.

video.title: What we prepare, and what to check before it goes out
video.summary: Your coach opens a finished piece of prepared work, reads it the way you should, and shows what to check before anything goes out under your name.

nodes.evidence: Your resume and LinkedIn lead with the role you want.

nodes.title: Show you can catch what AI gets wrong
nodes.why: Anyone can generate an app now. A dated audit of a real AI-built app, with the fixes, shows the judgment teams are hiring for, and a stranger can check it.

because: In your resume, there are no numbers that show the impact of your work.

nodes.prepared: We give you the audit checklist, a report outline, where to find an AI-built app whose owner wants it checked, and a note to send them.

stages.label: Gathering where to find an app
Drafting your note to the owner

tasks.title: Audit it against the checklist and fix the critical findings
tasks.done_when: Each critical finding is fixed and checked.
tasks.changed: A real AI-built app has a dated audit, with its critical findings fixed.

tasks.title: Publish the one-page audit report and link it at the top of your resume
tasks.done_when: The report is live and linked at the top of your resume.
tasks.changed: A reviewer can now open your audit from the top of your resume.

video.title: What we prepare, and what to check before it goes out
video.summary: Your coach opens a finished piece of prepared work, reads it the way you should, and shows what to check before anything goes out under your name.

nodes.evidence: One verified audit is linked at the top of your resume.
